verdicts.reading: Between 2000 and 2015 WMD (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) would come to be used, or be more likely to be used, against the US homeland or US forces and interests abroad than before 2000.
verdicts.mainstream_test: State of affairs (D30): at least one WMD use against the US or US forces 2000-2015, with risk rising versus the 1990s baseline (no such use in the 1990s).
verdicts.reason: Anthrax letters (Sept-Oct 2001) killed 5 in the US; chlorine car/truck bombs in Iraq hit US forces in 2007 (62 soldiers sickened at a Diyala base). No WMD use against the US in the 1990s, so realized use rose. Read as an expectation, not a possibility-only hedge; graded on realized use.

evidence.title: 2001 anthrax attacks
evidence.shows: Biological attack via mail on US senators and media, 5 deaths, 17 infected.

evidence.title: Chlorine bombings in Iraq
evidence.shows: Chlorine bombs 2006-2007; 3 June 2007 attack outside a US base in Diyala sickened at least 62 soldiers.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 the US would remain unmatched by any state or organization in combined economic, technological, military and diplomatic influence.
verdicts.mainstream_test: US first in nominal GDP, military spending and leading technology in 2015.
verdicts.reason: In 2015 US GDP (~18tn USD) was the largest; US military spending was about three times China's; US firms led global technology.

evidence.title: List of countries by military expenditures (SIPRI data)
evidence.shows: US 954bn USD, 33% of world military spending; China 336bn, 12%; US has led by a wide margin every year since 2000.

evidence.title: World Bank GDP (current US$)
evidence.shows: US GDP largest in the world in 2015, ahead of China.

verdicts.reading: Europe and Japan would need more than 110 million additional workers by 2015 to hold their 2000 dependency ratios.
verdicts.mainstream_test: A public measure of the workers needed to hold dependency ratios at the 2000 level, for 2015.
verdicts.reason: The claim is a model-derived requirement, not an outcome. No public series measures 'workers needed to hold the 2000 dependency ratio' in 2015; the UN Replacement Migration study (2000) is the only comparable calculation and is itself a projection.

evidence.title: UN DESA, Replacement Migration
evidence.shows: Model calculations of migrants needed to hold support ratios; no 2015 measured outcome of this quantity. Looked also at Eurostat and OECD labour series: they measure workers, not the requirement.

verdicts.reading: In 2015 Russia would be internally weak and tied to the international system mainly through its UN Security Council permanent seat.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Russia economically weak in 2015 and its main institutional link the UNSC seat.
verdicts.reason: Economically weak in 2015 (GDP -3.7%, junk credit rating, sanctions, G8 suspension 2014), so UNSC seat was its main remaining Western-facing lever. But Russia was not institutionally weak: centralised state, Crimea annexation, Syria intervention 2015; it was also in WTO (2012), G20, BRICS, SCO. Half the claim holds.

evidence.title: Russian financial crisis (2014-2016)
evidence.shows: GDP contracted 3.7% in 2015; S&P and Moody's cut Russia to junk; Western sanctions after Crimea.

verdicts.reason: World Bank 2015 population 1.328 billion: 'more than 1.2 billion' holds; 1.2 vs 1.33 is 9.6% off. India was the fastest-growing major economy and a rising power.

verdicts.reason: Market rates: world real GDP +71% (2020) / +76% (2019); implied level 87.4tn vs actual 83.1tn = 5% off (hit). Per capita +34%; implied level 11,820 vs 10,575 = 12% off (partial). At PPP both near target (+88%, +47%). Per-capita half partial at market rates.
